questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The most popular breakfast foods in the UK
How to cook a quick breakfast before work
Why coffee is bad for you in the morning
Why some experts think a big breakfast helps
questions.why: They ask how important breakfast is and hear why experts recommend eating a big one.

questions.q: What did Phil have for breakfast, and how does he feel now?
options: A pastry and coffee; he feels full
Porridge at six o'clock; he's hungry again
Nothing; he skipped it
Eggs and toast; he feels tired
questions.why: Phil had a big bowl of porridge at six o'clock, so he's hungry again now.

questions.q: What does Professor Alexandra Johnstone recommend?
options: Eating a big breakfast and a small dinner
Eating only two meals a day
Skipping breakfast to lose weight
Eating the same amount at every meal
questions.why: She supports 'breakfast like a king and dine like a pauper': big breakfast, small dinner.

questions.q: According to Alexandra, who is breakfast especially important for?
options: Children and teenagers who are still growing
Athletes who train early in the morning
People trying to stay healthy or lose weight
People who work at night and sleep all day
questions.why: She says it's important particularly for people maintaining a healthy weight or trying to lose weight.

questions.q: According to Courtney Peterson, what happens when we eat a large meal early in the day?
options: The body processes it better, with less sugar rise
We feel sleepy and tired for the rest of the day
We burn far fewer calories during the day
Our blood sugar rises much higher than usual
questions.why: She says the body is better at metabolising it, and blood sugar levels won't spike as high.

questions.q: Why does Courtney give the example of a bowl of ice cream?
options: To show that ice cream is actually healthy
To suggest eating dessert for breakfast instead
To explain why people love sweet food at night
The same food affects blood sugar more later
questions.why: Eaten in the afternoon or evening, the same ice cream makes blood sugar spike significantly higher.

questions.q: What are two reasons mentioned for why people skip breakfast?
options: They don't like the taste or they feel sick
Doctors tell them to, or they're on holiday
They don't have time, or they want to save money
They sleep late, or they exercise
questions.why: Phil says people skip it sometimes because they lack time and sometimes to save money.

questions.q: What does Alexandra's research suggest about people who eat breakfast regularly?
options: They eat more later in the day to make up
They're leaner and control their appetite better
They have much more energy for sport
They sleep better and longer at night
questions.why: She says regular breakfast eaters are leaner and a big morning meal gives better appetite control.
